narrative.overview: palico is a delightful little utility that lives on your desk — a warm, personable image toolkit you reach for without thinking. It is the opposite of the ad-laden converter sites it competes with: no banner ads, no fake download buttons, no cold enterprise chrome. The whole surface is bathed in warm cream, text is a soft espresso brown rather than hard black, corners are barely rounded, and shadows are gentle and warm-tinted. Typography is a single voice — Nunito throughout — leaning on weight and scale to carry character rather than a second display face. The result is friendly and highly legible without tipping into childishness. The system rejects sketchy converter sites, cold enterprise SaaS, and flashy over-animation. Warmth is the differentiator, and the tool disappears into the task — personality is reserved for moments, not sprayed across every control.
keyCharacteristics: Warm cream surfaces with espresso-brown ink, never pure white or pure black.
A single muted caramel accent — used for actions and state, not decoration.
A single typeface — Nunito across the whole product, with weight and scale doing the heavy lifting.
Tight, near-square radii (0–4px) and soft, warm-tinted shadows.
Privacy and trust are felt through restraint and clarity, not claimed in fine print.

rules.name: The One Warm Accent Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one accent — Muted Caramel. It marks actions, selection, and focus. It is never used for decoration, and never appears on inactive states.

rules.name: The No-Pure-Black, No-Pure-White Rule
rules.body: Text is Espresso Ink, never #000. Surfaces are Cream or Card Cream, never #fff. Pure neutrals read as cold and break the warmth.

rules.name: The Stoplight Rule
rules.body: Brick Red is reserved for destruction and error. Seeing it anywhere else is a bug.

rules.name: The One-Family Rule
rules.body: Every piece of text is Nunito. There is no second display face — if a hero feels flat, raise the weight to 900 and the scale, don't reach for another typeface.

rules.name: The Weight-Earns-Emphasis Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is established by weight and scale, not by color, italics, or decoration. Body 400, titles 600, headlines 700, display 900.

rules.name: The Fixed-Scale Rule
rules.body: Outside the hero, type sizes are fixed rem values, not fluid clamps.

rules.name: The Warm-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every shadow is tinted warm brown (hsl(28 13% 20%)), never neutral gray or black.

dos: Do surface the offline/on-device guarantee as a first-class part of the interface — privacy is visible, not buried.
Do keep one job, few clicks per tool; sensible defaults, advanced options tucked away until wanted.
Do use Espresso Ink on Cream/Card Cream for text, and verify Muted Ink hits ≥4.5:1 before using it for body copy.
Do tint every shadow warm brown (hsl(28 13% 20%)).
Do keep typography single-family — Nunito everywhere — and use weight (400/600/700/900) to step the hierarchy.
Do give every control a real focus-visible state (3px caramel ring) and a prefers-reduced-motion alternative.
donts: Don't evoke ad-heavy converter sites: no fake/disguised download buttons, no upload-to-server ambiguity, no popups or dark patterns.
Don't drift into cold enterprise SaaS: no navy-and-gray, no pure-white/pure-black, no soulless density.
Don't over-animate — motion conveys state, never spectacle. No orchestrated page-load sequences.
Don't use Brick Red for anything but destruction and error.
Don't hardcode off-palette colors like orange-300/emerald-300 (as the current home tiles do) — ground everything in the warm tokens.
Don't nest cards, or use a border-left/border-right colored stripe as a card or alert accent.
Don't introduce a second typeface for brand moments — if a hero needs more weight, push the Nunito Display tier (900 + larger scale), don't reach for a display face.
